content:
We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a tolyl (para methyl phenyl) attached to sulfonamide linking to another phenyl with a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl-para-phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-phenyl-NH (anilide). Actually the amide attaches to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N) meaning the amide nitrogen is attached to an aniline (anilide). So the target is a sulfonamide linking two phenyl rings, one with methyl, the other with a cinnamoyl anilide.

We need to propose a route with commercially available leaves, total cost under $9999, max 3 steps.

We need to use templates. We can search for retrosynthetic templates that break sulfonamide bond (S-N) and amide bond (C=O-N). Also maybe the double bond formation via Heck or Wittig.

Simplify: Could disassemble into three building blocks: (1) p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (or p-tolyl sulfonic acid) to form sulfonamide with aniline (or phenyl). Actually the sulfonamide is between p-tolyl-sulfonyl group and the second phenyl (the one bearing the cinnamoyl). So we could start from p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (commercial) and the aniline (the second phenyl) to make sulfonamide. Then we need to attach the cinnamoyl amide onto that phenyl (the sulfonyl phenyl). That could be via acylation of aniline (the same aniline) with trans-cinnamoyl chloride (or trans-cinnamic acid via coupling). So maybe route: Step 1: Form sulfonamide between p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and 4-aminophenyl (the phenyl that will later be acylated). Step 2: Acylate the remaining aniline (the same nitrogen) with trans-cinnamoyl chloride to give amide. However the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the sulfonyl group, not the aniline. Wait the sulfonamide is NS(=O)(=O) attached to the p-tolyl ring on one side, and attached to the second phenyl ring on the other side (the phenyl bearing the cinnamoyl). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the second phenyl (as an aniline). That second phenyl also has an amide substituent (C=O-NH-Ph-NH2). Actually the amide is attached to the second phenyl via a carbonyl attached to the double bond chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2. So the second phenyl has a substituent: -CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2. The sulfonamide nitrogen attaches directly to the phenyl ring (i.e., the phenyl is attached to N). So the phenyl is an aniline (attached to N). That aniline also has the cinnamoyl amide attached at para position? Let's examine SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to NS(=O)(=O) from the first phenyl. So the second phenyl has the substituent at para position relative to the sulfonamide? The SMILES: c2ccc( ... )cc2, with NS(=O)(=O) attached to that phenyl at position 1 (the N). So the phenyl is N-sulfonyl aniline (i.e., sulfonamide). At para position, there is the cinnamoyl amide chain.

Thus we can think of building block: p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (commercial) + 4-aminophenyl (p-aminophenyl) to make sulfonamide (N-sulfonyl aniline). Then we need to functionalize the para position of that aniline with a trans-cinnamoyl amide. That could be via a Suzuki coupling of a para-bromo substituent with a vinyl amide, or via a Heck reaction of a para-iodo phenyl sulfonamide with trans-cinnamyl acrylate? Simpler: Use a para-bromo sulfonamide (starting from p-bromo aniline) then do a Suzuki coupling with a vinyl boronic acid bearing amide? Might be complex.

Alternative route: Build the cinnamoyl amide first on aniline, then sulfonylate the aniline nitrogen. That is, start with 4-aminophenyl (p-aminophenyl) that is also para-substituted with the cinnamoyl amide. So we need to install the cinnamoyl amide onto the aniline (para position). Could start from 4-bromo aniline, do a Suzuki coupling with trans-cinnamoyl boronic acid? Not typical. Could do a Friedel-Crafts acylation of aniline? Not good.

Maybe easier: Use a three-step route: Step 1: Synthesize trans-cinnamoyl anilide (i.e., trans-cinnamoyl chloride + aniline). That gives C6H5-NH-CO-CH=CH-Ph. Then step 2: Sulfonylate the aniline nitrogen of that product with p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride to give the sulfonamide. However the aniline nitrogen is already part of amide (C=O-NH-). Wait the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl (c3ccccc3N). Actually the amide is C(=O)N-Ph-NH2 (i.e., the amide nitrogen attached to phenyl which has an NH2 group). So there are two nitrogens on that phenyl: one is the amide nitrogen (attached to carbonyl) and the other is an aniline NH2 (free). The sulfonamide attaches to the aniline NH2 (the free NH2). So we need a phenyl with both an amide substituent and a free NH2 that can be sulfonylated. So we could start from 4-aminophenyl (p-aminophenyl) and first acylate the para position (i.e., the aromatic ring) with trans-cinnamoyl group via a Friedel-Crafts acylation? Not typical for aromatic substitution with unsaturated acyl.

Alternative: Use a Suzuki coupling to attach the cinnamoyl chain onto the phenyl after sulfonamide formation. For example, start with p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride + 4-bromo aniline to make sulfonamide with bromo substituent para to N. Then do a Heck coupling with trans-cinnamyl acrylate? Actually we need to attach /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2. Could do a Suzuki coupling of the bromo phenyl sulfonamide with a vinyl boronic acid that has a carbonyl amide attached to an aniline. That seems complex.

Maybe we can propose a route using three steps: 1) Prepare sulfonamide from p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and 4-aminophenyl (commercial). 2) Perform a Suzuki coupling of the para-bromo derivative (so we need bromo on phenyl). So we could start with p-bromo-4-aminophenyl? Actually we need a bromo on the phenyl that will be sulfonylated. So start with 4-bromo-2-methylaniline? Wait p-tolyl is separate. The sulfonyl group is attached to p-tolyl ring, not the other phenyl. So we need the second phenyl to have a bromo at para position relative to sulfonamide nitrogen. So we could start with 4-bromo-2-aminobenzenesulfonyl? Not.

Simplify: Use three steps: (1) Synthesize the sulfonamide using p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and 4-aminophenyl (commercial). (2) Perform a Suzuki coupling of the resulting sulfonamide (which still has a hydrogen at para position) with a vinyl boronic acid that carries the amide side chain. But we need a leaving group on the phenyl to couple. So we need to start with 4-bromo-4-aminophenyl? Actually we need a bromine at para position to the sulfonamide nitrogen. So we could start with 4-bromo-2-aminobenzenesulfonyl? Wait the sulfonamide nitrogen attaches to the phenyl; the phenyl originally is aniline (NH2). So we could start with 4-bromo-2-aminobenzenesulfonyl? Not.

Better: Use a two-step route: Step 1: Form sulfonamide between p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and 4-aminophenyl (commercial). This yields N-(4-aminophenyl)-p-tolylsulfonamide (the target phenyl still has NH2). Step 2: Acylate that NH2 with trans-cinnamoyl chloride to give the final product. This is just two steps! Indeed the amide is attached to the same aniline nitrogen that is also sulfonylated? Wait the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the phenyl, not the aniline nitrogen. The phenyl has the sulfonamide nitrogen attached to it (i.e., the phenyl is attached to N). The phenyl also has an NH2 group (the aniline) that is acylated. In the SMILES, the phenyl with the sulfonamide is "c2ccc(... )cc2" and the sulfonamide is "NS(=O)(=O)" attached to that phenyl. The amide side chain is attached to the phenyl at para position: "/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N". The amide nitrogen is attached to another phenyl which has an NH2 (c3ccccc3N). So the amide nitrogen is attached to a phenyl with an NH2 substituent (an aniline). So there are two phenyl rings: phenyl A (p-tolyl) attached to sulfonyl group; phenyl B (the central phenyl) attached to sulfonamide nitrogen and to the cinnamoyl amide chain; phenyl C (the terminal phenyl) attached to the amide nitrogen and has an NH2.

Thus the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to phenyl B (central). The amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl C (terminal) which also has an NH2 group (maybe para to amide). Actually the SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N indicates an aniline with NH2 at para? Wait "Nc3ccccc3N" is an aniline where the nitrogen is attached to the phenyl (as substituent) and there is another NH2 on the phenyl (the trailing N). So phenyl C has two substituents: one is the amide nitrogen (attached to carbonyl) and the other is an NH2 (free). So phenyl C is 4-aminophenyl attached via amide.

Thus the route could be: Step 1: Synthesize phenyl C (4-aminophenyl) (commercial). Step 2: Form amide with trans-cinnamic acid (or acid chloride) to give trans-cinnamoyl-4-aminophenyl (i.e., C(=O)N-Ph-NH2). That's the amide side chain. Step 3: Couple this amide side chain to phenyl B via a Suzuki coupling? Actually the side chain is attached via a double bond to phenyl B: /C=C/ attached to phenyl B at para position. So we need to form a carbon-carbon double bond linking phenyl B to the carbonyl carbon of the amide side chain. This could be done via a Heck reaction between phenyl B (with a bromine at para) and trans-cinnamoyl amide (as an alkene). But the side chain is an α,β-unsaturated amide (cinnamoyl). So we could start with phenyl B (para-bromo) and do a Suzuki coupling with a vinyl boronic acid that is attached to the amide side chain (i.e., (E)-3-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamide). That vinyl boronic acid may not be commercially available.

Alternative: Use a three-step route: (1) Form sulfonamide between p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and 4-bromo-2-aminophenyl? Actually we need phenyl B to have a bromine at para to allow coupling later. So start with 4-bromo-2-aminobenzenesulfonyl? Wait the sulfonamide nitrogen attaches to phenyl B, not the sulfonyl group. So we need phenyl B with an amine (NH2) to react with sulfonyl chloride to give sulfonamide. So we need 4-bromo-2-aminobenzene (i.e., 4-bromo-aniline). That's commercially available (p-bromoaniline). Then react with p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride to give N-(p-tolylsulfonyl)-4-bromoaniline (i.e., sulfonamide with bromine para). Then perform Suzuki coupling of that bromine with a vinyl boronic acid that carries the amide side chain (maybe (E)-3-(4-aminophenyl)acrylic acid boronic ester). Might be not commercial.

Maybe we can propose a route using three steps: (1) Prepare sulfonamide as above. (2) Perform a Heck coupling with trans-cinnamyl amide (i.e., trans-cinnamoyl chloride + 4-aminophenyl) to attach the double bond directly onto the phenyl B. Actually Heck coupling uses aryl halide (bromo) with alkene (cinnamyl). So we could have phenyl B brominated, then Heck with trans-cinnamoyl amide (as an alkene). The alkene is the trans-cinnamoyl amide (C=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2). That could be used as the alkene partner. So we need trans-cinnamoyl amide (the terminal phenyl with amide). That could be synthesized separately (step 2) from 4-aminophenyl and trans-cinnamic acid (or acid chloride). Then step 3: Heck coupling between bromophenyl sulfonamide and the trans-cinnamoyl amide alkene to give final product.

Thus total steps: 1) Synthesize sulfonamide from p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride + p-bromoaniline. 2) Synthesize trans-cinnamoyl amide from trans-cinnamic acid (or acid chloride) + 4-aminophenyl. 3) Heck coupling between the two to form the C=C bond.

All leaves: p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (commercial), p-bromoaniline (commercial), trans-cinnamic acid (commercial), 4-aminophenyl (i.e., aniline) (commercial). All likely under $10k.

Now we need to find templates for sulfonamide formation (S-N bond formation) and amide formation (C=O-N) and Heck coupling (C-C bond formation with alkene). Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria to find appropriate template IDs.

First, get available functional groups list to know correct names.
